messages:
liz: Heads up — scheduling a rolling reboot + graceful evacuation for rack r10 (us-east1) due to repeated thermal sensor spikes. Window: Wed 03:00-06:00 UTC. Primary goals: avoid pod loss, keep latency SLOs, and minimize reserved capacity impact. Posting runbook in a minute.

amar: ETA on when you need apps drained by? can we do a 30m grace period per node? @kevin are there any streaming jobs that need special handling?

sanjay: Plan proposal: cordon cohort r10 nodes, then sequentially drain with 30m grace where possible. For critical streaming jobs we’ll mark pods with node.kubernetes.io/maintenance=true to trigger early failover policies. If grace expires, run:

```
kubectl cordon node-XXX
kubectl drain node-XXX --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=1800 --timeout=35m
```

Don’t use --force. We should preserve local SSD data where possible.

kevin: Dedicated GPU pools (redwood-dedicated-*) are NOT on r10; only shared-gpu pool is impacted. Streaming infra (kinesis consumers) has 2x replicas across us-east1-a/b — we need to avoid draining both a/b at once. Suggest cohort ordering: r10-a then r10-b.

liz: Agree on ordering. I set a 30m grace per node. Ops note: if any pod blocks for >20m, add the annotation team/evac-wait and we’ll triage.

amar: Backfill plan: spawn 4 temporary shared-gpu nodes in us-east1-c to soak jobs during ramp, then let scheduler rebalance. Cost hit estimate ~low but call it out in finance thread. Do we have quota? @ops-bot can you precheck?

ops-bot: Maintenance ticket MH-3821 created. Quota check: available GPUs in us-east1-c = 6. Auto reminders set at 60m and 10m before window.

liz: Thanks. To reduce cross-region traffic, prefer local backfill before falling back to us-west1. If latency-sensitive endpoints degrade, route policy will failover to us-west1 read replicas — ops will flip if 2xx p50 > 200ms for 5m.

kevin: Quick note on canaries: Turn off canary autoscaling for models-heavy endpoints during the window, otherwise new instances may land on drained nodes. I’ll push a short config:

```yaml
canary_autoscale: disabled
routing_hint: us-east1-c
```

liz: Monitoring checklist (we’ll watch these during the window): node_temp_95p, node_evictions, pod_restart_rate, queue_latency, token-gen-latency. Pager rules: node_temp_95p -> oncall; pod_evictions >3/min -> infra-alert.

amar: If any pod has critical PII jobs, please tag so we can ticket for non-disruptive migration.

sanjay: Post-maint steps: uncordon nodes with a 5m soak:

```
kubectl uncordon node-XXX
# verify pod readiness and KV cache warmup
```

Also kick a prefix cache warmup job for top-20 models after each node returns.

liz: I’ll post the runbook link here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/r10-thermal-maint (watch-only link). I also added the escalation list. If thermal spikes continue after reboots we’ll extend to 09:00 UTC and notify customers.

kevin: Thx. I’ll chair the ops channel during window. If anything urgent ping me directly. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: Wed 02:00 UTC and Wed 02:50 UTC.

liz: Great. Final ask — teams, please drain long-running debug sessions (notebooks) by EOD so users aren’t surprised. I’ll post an update 1h before window starts. :calendar:
